title: QUIZ - 21
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Finding the Constant of Inverse Proportionality
questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant k for an inverse variation relationship
questions.question: A quantity y varies inversely with x (y = k/x). When x = 7, y = 9. What is the constant k?
questions.explanation: Since \(y = k/x, k = x \times y = 7 \times 9 = 63\).
questions.hint: For inverse proportionality y = k/x, the constant k equals x multiplied by y.

questions.concept: Recognizing Inverse Proportion from a Table
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a table of values represents an inverse proportion
questions.question: Does the following set of (x, y) pairs represent an inverse proportion? (1, 7), (2, 11), (3, 17), (4, 26)

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because x times y is the same constant value for every pair.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because y decreases as x increases, regardless of the values.

options.label: C
options.text: It cannot be determined from a table of values.

options.label: D
options.text: No, because x times y is not the same for every pair.

questions.explanation: Checking x times y for each pair: \(1 \times 7 = 7, 2 \times 11 = 22, 3 \times 17 = 51, 4 \times 26 = 104\). These products are not all equal, so this is not an inverse proportion.
questions.hint: An inverse proportion requires x times y to be the same constant for every pair.

questions.concept: Predicting Values Using Inverse Proportionality
questions.learningObjective: Use a known inverse-proportion pair to predict a new value
questions.question: The pressure of a gas varies inversely with its volume at constant temperature. If x = 7 gives y = 5, what is y when x = 5?
questions.explanation: Since xy is constant for inverse variation, \(k = 7 \times 5 = 35\). When x = 5, y = 35/5 = 7.
questions.hint: In inverse proportionality, x times y stays constant.
